slides.title: SkillMoV: Mixture-of-View Routing with Prototype-Conditioned Gating for Unified Multi-View Proficiency Estimation
slides.tldr: MULTI-VIEW HUMAN PROFICIENCY ESTIMATION
slides.highlight: SkillMoV introduces a Mixture-of-View Projector to estimate human proficiency from synchronized ego and exo-view videos, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on multi-view skill estimation.

card.one_liner: SkillMoV is a parameter-efficient framework for unified multi-view human proficiency estimation using expert-based view routing.
card.key_idea: A Mixture-of-View Projector (MoVP) uses soft routing for camera-specific features, cross-view attention, prototype anchoring, and prototype-conditioned gated projection to handle heterogeneous viewpoints.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on EgoExo4D across six skill domains; achieved 50.17% accuracy in the Exos setting, surpassing the strongest reported baseline by 3.57 percentage points.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in Ego-only settings (40.00%) as the architecture is specifically designed for multi-view routing and aggregation.

slides.title: Alibaba Launches Qwen-Robot Series Embodied AI Large Models
slides.tldr: ALIBABA RELEASES QWEN-ROBOT EMBODIED AI MODELS
slides.highlight: Alibaba has launched the Qwen-Robot series of embodied AI large models, providing relevant developments for RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Strategies for preventing and reversing polarized online discourse
slides.tldr: MODELING POLARIZED ONLINE DISCOURSE
slides.highlight: This research develops a psychology-based computational model of opinion dynamics, providing insights for MIMIC's simulation of societal-scale impact and harmonious human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Psychology-based computational modeling shows that amplifying moderate elites is most effective at reversing online polarization.
card.key_idea: A model using multi-dimensional identities, memory, and utility-based attitude updates to test interventions like attention nudges, norm enforcement, and the 'Overton window'.
card.evaluation: Large-scale simulations (N=100) over 20-50 year equivalent timescales, varying parameters like attention bias and in-group pull to classify discourse states.
card.limitation: Once polarization occurs, interventions can result in 'latent extremism' when individuals possess complex, multi-dimensional identities.

slides.title: MuVAP: Multimodal Multiparty Voice Activity Projection for Turn-taking Prediction in the Wild
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL TURN-TAKING PREDICTION
slides.highlight: MuVAP uses a causal multimodal framework to predict speaker-aware turn-taking from a single camera and monaural audio, supporting HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: MuVAP predicts turn-taking in multiparty conversations using a single camera and monaural audio stream.
card.key_idea: A causal framework using Role-Relative Projection to map N-speaker dynamics onto a fixed 'current vs. next' state, grounding acoustic predictions in visual face tracks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new 31-hour AVCC dataset using Macro-F1 for Shift-Hold and accuracy for Next Speaker Prediction; outperformed MLP baselines.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in 'active' prediction tasks compared to 'silent' ones and decreases as the number of speakers increases.

slides.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Abilities for Addressee, Turn-change, and Next Speaker Prediction in Meetings
slides.tldr: LLM EVALUATION FOR MEETING TURN-TAKING
slides.highlight: This research evaluates LLMs and multimodal LLMs on addressee detection and speaker prediction, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and team state perception.

card.one_liner: LLMs outperform humans and supervised models in next speaker prediction for multi-party meetings using conversational context.
card.key_idea: A unified framework comparing supervised models, text-based LLMs, and MM-LLMs on addressee detection, turn-change prediction, and next speaker prediction using the AMI corpus.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the AMI corpus using accuracy and F1 scores; compared against supervised baselines and human subjects (non-native English speakers).
card.limitation: MM-LLMs struggle to effectively leverage raw audio-visual signals, and human evaluation was limited to non-native English speakers.

slides.title: Beyond Usability: A UX Case Study on Using "Withdrawal Design" to Challenge Engagement Metrics in Social Robotics
slides.tldr: CHALLENGING ENGAGEMENT METRICS IN SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: This study examines how the removal of a social robot can prompt children with autism to seek human interaction, suggesting that high engagement may sometimes silo social behavior. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Withdrawal of social robots may better promote human interaction than continuous engagement for children with autism.
card.key_idea: A mixed-methods randomized controlled trial comparing continuous robot access versus robot withdrawal to evaluate effects on social motivation and human-centric interaction.
card.evaluation: 8-week home trial (N=40) using SCARED, RCADS, SMS, RMET, and SUS metrics. Results show a trade-off between anxiety reduction and social motivation.
card.limitation: Continuous robot use may silo social behavior within the child-robot dyad, potentially masking ecological downsides of high engagement.

slides.title: Bidirectional Tutoring for Developmental Motor Learning in Robots: Co-Developed Interaction Dynamics Support Stable Learning
slides.tldr: BIDIRECTIONAL TUTORING FOR ROBOT MOTOR LEARNING
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that bidirectional tutoring, where robots and tutors dynamically adapt to each other, fosters more consistent behavioral patterns and stable motor learning than unidirectional interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Bidirectional tutoring improves robot motor learning by co-developing trajectories that preserve behavioral coherence and support generalization.
card.key_idea: A FEP-based neural network (PV-RNN) with generative replay learns from interactive tutoring where the tutor intervenes in the robot's active behavior rather than providing passive demonstrations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a humanoid robot performing object manipulation across 10 phases. Bidirectional tutoring achieved significantly higher success rates (up to 90%) than unidirectional tutoring.
card.limitation: The human-tutoring experiment was a proof-of-concept conducted by a single experimenter, limiting the diversity of human tutoring styles.

slides.title: A Causal Model of Theory of Mind in Conflict for Artificial Intelligence
slides.tldr: CAUSAL MODEL FOR SELECTIVE ToM ENGAGEMENT
slides.highlight: This work proposes a structural causal model to determine when AI should engage Theory of Mind (ToM) during conflict, supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of inferring partner intent via ToM.

card.one_liner: A structural causal model determining when AI should engage Theory of Mind (ToM) during conflict.
card.key_idea: A DAG-based framework treating ToM as a resource-rational mechanism triggered by information asymmetry, low solution tractability, and perceived sophistication mismatches between agents.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper provides a theoretical framework and structural equations, noting that simulation and empirical validation are for future work.
card.limitation: The model is currently static and dyadic, and several functional forms for variables remain unspecified and require empirical calibration.

slides.title: Generating Natural and Expressive Robot Gestures through Iterative Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback using LLMs
slides.tldr: RLHF-TUNED LLM GESTURE GENERATION FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research utilizes RLHF and LLMs to generate more expressive and fluid co-speech gestures for the Pepper humanoid robot, enhancing human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and HRI.

card.one_liner: Iterative RLHF improves the expressiveness, relevance, and fluidity of LLM-generated co-speech gestures for humanoid robots.
card.key_idea: GPT-4 generates motion code from a primitive function library, refined through five iterations of offline Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and online few-shot prompting using human ratings.
card.evaluation: 250 participants rated videos of Pepper robot across five iterations. Results showed statistically significant improvements (p<0.001) in expressiveness, relevance, and fluidity.
card.limitation: Relying on low-level primitives can lead to mode collapse, repetitive patterns, and difficulty sustaining gesture diversity.

slides.title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
slides.tldr: SYNCHRONIZED CO-SPEECH GESTURES FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: WaveSync uses a hybrid framework and wavefront optimization to align expressive gestures with speech while ensuring kinematic feasibility. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: WaveSync synchronizes humanoid robot gestures with speech emphasis while respecting strict physical kinematic constraints.
card.key_idea: An LLM generates a Semantic Importance Wave; Dynamic Movement Primitives shape trajectories, and a Wavefront Optimizer aligns gesture peaks to speech peaks using duration compression and forward propagation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via PyBullet simulations across five scenarios using objective metrics (HbS, PAM, Jerk) and subjective Likert ratings from 20 participants; outperformed three ablated baselines.
card.limitation: The system relies on a fixed action library, which limits its ability to handle unconstrained dialogue.

slides.title: SCAN: A Decision-Making Framework for Effective Task Allocation with Generative AI
slides.tldr: HUMAN-CENTRIC GENAI TASK ALLOCATION FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: SCAN introduces a framework for task allocation based on metacognition and the Zone of Proximal Development, supporting the ADAM-CHAT goal of developing AI teammates that align with human learning and collaboration.

card.one_liner: SCAN is a human-centric framework for allocating tasks between humans and GenAI to sustain lifelong learning.
card.key_idea: It uses Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development and metacognition to categorize tasks into four sub-zones: Substitute, Complement, Aid, and Non-negotiable.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated. The paper describes a theoretical framework and application scenarios rather than providing empirical experimental results.
card.limitation: Effective use depends on the user's metacognitive resolution; poor self-assessment can lead to misallocation, over-reliance, or automation bias.

slides.title: Fast When, Careful Who: Dual-Process Multiparty Turn-Taking with Diffusion Augmentation
slides.tldr: MULTIPARTY TURN-TAKING PIPELINE
slides.highlight: This work proposes a two-stage audio-only pipeline for multiparty turn-taking that separates boundary triggering from floor transfer verification, supporting HyECHO's focus on diarization and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: A dual-process audio pipeline for multiparty turn-taking using diffusion-based background augmentation to improve shift detection.
card.key_idea: A fast WavLM-based gate proposes turn boundaries, while a slow ECAPA-TDNN verifier confirms floor transfers (HOLD vs SHIFT) and predicts the next speaker via embedding similarity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VoxConverse using precision, recall, F1, and MAE. Outperformed a ResCNN-Siamese baseline and a dyadic VAP benchmark in shift detection.
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by boundary coverage, particularly in heavily overlapped or fast-exchange regions where acoustic cues are ambiguous.

slides.title: Co-Creating Buildable and Open Social Robot Study Companions with University Students
slides.tldr: CO-DESIGNING ACCESSIBLE OPEN-SOURCE SOCIAL ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how Design for Assembly and Disassembly can lower barriers for students building social robots, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: DfA and DfD mechanical redesigns significantly improve the usability and perceived buildability of open-source social robots.
card.key_idea: Applied the Double Diamond framework to redesign the Robot Study Companion (v4.1) using twist-lock fasteners, snap-fit joints, and tool-free service latches to reduce assembly friction.
card.evaluation: Two studies with developers and first-time builders using SUS, NASA-TLX, and assembly timing; SUS rose from 59.4 to 89.4 for developers.
card.limitation: Small, non-random samples and a lack of inter-rater reliability checks for thematic coding.

slides.title: Correct Yourself, Keep My Trust: How Self-Correction and Social Connection Shape Credibility in Social Chatbots
slides.tldr: SELF-CORRECTION PRESERVES CHATBOT CREDIBILITY
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that self-correction maintains trustworthiness and expertise better than external corrections, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction for human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Self-correction preserves a social chatbot's credibility and leverages social bonds to improve error correction effectiveness.
card.key_idea: Comparing self-correction against external sources (webpage/expert), the study found self-correction maintains trustworthiness and expertise while using social connection to amplify belief change.
card.evaluation: Between-subjects experiment (N=120) using 7-point Likert scales and ANOVA. Results are robust, supported by bootstrap confidence intervals and permutation tests.

slides.title: LLM-Mediated Human-AI Interaction in Search and Rescue: Impact of Expertise on Attentional Allocation
slides.tldr: LLM GUIDANCE IMPACTS ATTENTION AND EXPERTISE
slides.highlight: This research examines how LLM guidance affects attentional allocation and decision-making in search and rescue, providing insights into how AI teammates can be adapted to different levels of human expertise for ADAM-CHAT.

card.one_liner: LLM guidance improves search-and-rescue efficiency but shifts attention from the environment to the AI interface.
card.key_idea: A simulated SAR task comparing LLM-guided and no-LLM conditions, using eye-tracking and behavioral metrics to analyze how expertise affects attentional allocation and cognitive load.
card.evaluation: 13 participants; metrics included victims-per-step, total rewards, and eye-tracking (fixations, pupil size). Results showed improved efficiency but no increase in total victims saved.
card.limitation: Small sample size (13 participants) and a simulated grid-based environment may limit generalizability to real-world SAR scenarios.

slides.title: Click4Assistance Launches FIFA World Cup 2026 AI Agent Experience
slides.tldr: AI AGENT FOR FAN ENGAGEMENT
slides.highlight: The launch of an AI agent experience for fan engagement relates to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement within human-AI teams.

slides.title: Optimal Order of Multi-Agent and General Many-Body Systems
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING COLLECTIVE BEHAVIOR IN MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: This research provides a framework for analyzing how agent power and response functions influence macroscopic properties like order and fragility, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: A framework for optimizing collective behavior by balancing agent power and response functions to manage stability.
card.key_idea: Analyzes macroscopic properties (entropy, order, fragility) derived from agent-level power and response functions, using a risk-appetite utility function to find the optimal degree of order.
card.limitation: Stronger synchronization may increase collective output but risks increasing systemic fragility and reducing mobility.

slides.title: Self-Driving Negotiator: An interactive, verifiable benchmark for social negotiation and theory of mind under hidden intent
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR SOCIAL NEGOTIATION AND THEORY OF MIND IN DRIVING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for measuring implicit social coordination and the ability to infer hidden intent from behavior, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on theory of mind and adaptive human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: A text-based interactive benchmark measuring LLMs' ability to infer hidden driver intent via social negotiation.
card.key_idea: A multi-turn POMDP environment where agents must deduce latent dispositions (e.g., committed vs. yielding) from behavioral cues to coordinate safely without explicit communication.
card.evaluation: Six LLMs tested across three scenarios (yield, pedestrian, merge) using success rates and decision-correctness; results show models struggle compared to scripted experts.
card.limitation: The benchmark is text-only, deliberately omitting perception, visual processing, and low-level control layers of a full driving stack.

slides.title: Talking to Your Data: Exploring Embodied Conversation as an Interface for Personal Health Reflection
slides.tldr: EMBODIED CONVERSATIONAL INTERFACE FOR HEALTH DATA REFLECTION
slides.highlight: This work explores an embodied conversational agent that uses a dual-agent design to facilitate active sensemaking of health data, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: An embodied conversational agent helps users translate personal health data into concrete, actionable health plans.
card.key_idea: A dual-agent architecture (Observer for statistics, Presenter for dialogue) combined with a Unity-based 3D avatar to facilitate shared-view reflection of wearable health data.
card.evaluation: Within-subject pilot study (N=5) using simulated personas from LifeSnaps; compared dashboards vs. agent via Likert scales and a 3-point specificity score.
card.limitation: Small, homogeneous sample size; simulated personas lacked emotional stakes; some users found the 3D avatar visually distracting.

slides.title: Microsoft Launches Agentic AI System Copilot Cowork
slides.tldr: MICROSOFT LAUNCHES AGENTIC AI SYSTEM
slides.highlight: The launch of Copilot Cowork introduces an agentic AI system, providing a relevant example of AI agents designed for collaborative work environments for ADAM-CHAT.

slides.title: Video-Based Optimal Transport for Feedback-Efficient Offline Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: OPTIMAL TRANSPORT FOR EFFICIENT REWARD LEARNING
slides.highlight: This work introduces VOTP, which uses optimal transport to align visual trajectories and generate pseudo-labels, supporting the MOSAIC goal of aligning human-AI intent via Optimal Transport.

card.one_liner: VOTP improves offline preference-based RL efficiency by generating high-fidelity pseudo-labels using video foundation models.
card.key_idea: Uses optimal transport to align unlabeled video trajectories with a few labeled ones in a Video Foundation Model's latent space to propagate preference labels.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on D4RL locomotion and MetaWorld manipulation benchmarks; outperformed state-of-the-art offline PbRL baselines and matched Oracle performance in some tasks.
card.limitation: Performance depends on balancing the preference threshold to manage the trade-off between pseudo-label quality and quantity.

slides.title: iQanAI Launches Human-Like Agentic AI Sales Platform
slides.tldr: AGENTIC AI SALES PLATFORM LAUNCH
slides.highlight: The launch of a human-like agentic AI platform is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on developing adaptive AI teammates and agentic capabilities.
